newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe group slams government over strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe group slams government over strike.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government has fired about 11,000 nurses for defying an order to end a strike which has paralysed hospitals around the country.
Zimbabwe's main human rights watchdog, Zimrights, slammed the government, saying its heavy-handed tactics only worsen the crisis gripping the public health sector.

"Zimrights deplores the heavy-handed stance by the government in dealing with the issue of striking nurses and other civil servants. The stance will not resolve anything but worsen the health system which is almost collapsing," Zimrights said.

"Nurses are offering a vital service to the nation and so accordingly they have to be rewarded for their efforts. Dismissing strikers will not resolve the problems, it will only resurface in another form," it added in a statement.

Acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shamuyarira said the government would not rehire the nurses who stopped working on October 21 to press for higher salaries, allowances and negotiations on their working conditions.
"All the doctors and nurses who didn't turn up for duty this morning are fired," he told state media on Wednesday night.
"We are very serious this time. We will not tolerate strikes any more. People should just learn to negotiate," he added.

The nurses' strike has forced major state hospitals around the country to close several wards. Many of them have had to call in army and Red Cross medical personnel to help doctors who are handling emergencies only.

The official media said several people have died over the past week due to lack of health care. The Herald newspaper said in an editorial on Thursday that the nurses and doctors were betraying their oath to save lives.
Shamuyarira said the cash-strapped government was reinstating a year-end bonus, which it scrapped last year and was one of the key demands of the strikers.

Deputy Commissioner (Crime) Godwin Matanga said police had been instructed to arrest any nurses involved in a public gathering, displaying placards or wearing clothing with demonstration messages on them.
He said their strike was illegal. This was the second civil servant strike in two months although this time it only involved junior doctors and nurses and some teachers.
On Thursday morning, the fired nurses were nowhere to be found in the city centre as police continued to seal off a park in central Harare where they have been gathering.
Junior doctors who went back to work on Wednesday following the government's ultimatum said they were just sitting around at the hospitals because they could not work without the nurses.
